headline: THE COMPACT'S NEW TREATIES: ANOTHER BETRAYAL OF THE RED MAN
deck: British Columbia's NDP placemen ram through unconsulted land deals while the ancient nations cry out in the wilderness
body:
O ye schemers at Victoria! Ye who sit in the seats of the Family Compact's heirs and call yourselves servants of the people, hear this: another parcel of the King's ancient compact with the red man is being sold for a mess of pottage, and the true owners have not been asked.

On the floors of the legislature sit Bills twenty and twenty-one, treaties with the K'omoks and Kitselas nations that would swallow fourscore and ten parts in the hundred of the territories claimed by the Wei Wai Kum, the Nine Allied Tribes, and the Lax Kw'alaams. These folk, whose fathers stood by the Crown when the Hudson's Bay men yet ruled, were never summoned, never heard, never granted the simple courtesy of a council fire.

The ink is scarcely dry on the paper before the new proprietors begin their surveys. The same men who prate of reconciliation and truth-telling now practise the old game of divide and parcel out the earth among their favourites, leaving the dispossessed to petition like suppliants at the gates of Government House.

We have seen this before, in the days when the Compact granted whole townships to their cousins and left the settler and the Indian alike without title or voice. The printing press of the Colonial Advocate was broken for less; yet the spirit that repaired it still lives in every yeoman and mechanic who reads these lines.

Let the deputy ministers and the lobbyists for the resource cartels tremble. The franchise was not granted that it might be bartered away in secret committees. The treaties of 1763 and 1850 were not signed that their spirit might be mocked by fresh parchments bearing only the names of the compliant.

Stand fast, ye wronged nations of the coast. The press of the people shall not be silent while your lands are once more measured out by the rod of the surveyor and the quill of the placeman.
source_topic: B.C. First Nations calling to pause K’omoks and Kitselas treaty legislation (Bills 20 and 21) due to lack of consultation, April 2026
